meta._provenance: code-to-figma skill; schema from the reference programme's flow-edges.json
meta.rule: Every line in Figma is generated from this file. Never draw one by hand, never edit one by hand. To change the flow, change this file and regenerate. If a frame moves, delete all lines and regenerate — do not repair them.

layout._comment: grid placement: x = originX + col * xPitch, y = originY + row * yPitch

edgeKinds._comment: These six cover every router: a user did something, a guard decided, the system moved itself, something failed and moved, something failed and stayed, someone went back. Draw each kind distinctly and put a legend on the canvas.
edgeKinds.action: solid, foreground colour — the user tapped or submitted something
edgeKinds.guard: dashed, muted — a redirect guard decided this from session or auth state; no button involved
edgeKinds.auto: dashed, muted — the system moves itself (timer, auto-submit, forward-on-success)
edgeKinds.failure: solid, danger colour — a failure branch that changes screen
edgeKinds.selfFailure: danger self-loop — failed but stayed on the same screen (dialog or inline error)
edgeKinds.back: thin solid, reverse direction — back button or system back

nodes._comment: One per screen. `class` is the code identifier and must equal the Figma frame name. `file` cites where the route is declared, with a line number. col/row place it on the grid.

guardNode._comment: OPTIONAL — only if the app has a central redirect guard. Delete if not. `decisions` lists what the guard does per state; `to: null` means allowed through.
guardNode.label: {{RedirectGuardName}}

edges._comment: `label` is the user-facing caption drawn on the arrow. `condition` is the code-level predicate. `src` is mandatory — an edge with no source line is a guess. `highlight: true` flags a genuinely dangerous path.
edges.label: {{what the user did}}

outOfFlowEdges._comment: Entries and exits that cross the boundary of this flow. Drawn to a stub, not to a frame.
